what: Figure (A) — printed at the foot of the right-hand column of p-57, below the Q2 instruction. A cartoon of dark clouds raining heavily straight down over a plain, with two magenta arrows pointing vertically UPWARD through the rain to show the rising heated air. This is the convectional-rainfall picture; Q2 asks the student to name the rainfall type each picture shows, so it needs this figure together with Figures (B) and (C) on the next page.

Figures (B) and (C) — the other two pictures of the same Q2 set, stacked in the left-hand column of p-58. Figure (B): a cross-section of a mountain, moisture-laden wind blowing in from a water body on the left, heavy rain from dark clouds on the windward (left) slope and a small isolated cloud with light rain beyond the leeward (right) slope — orographic rainfall. Figure (C): a spiral cyclone seen from above with blue arrows entering the left and leaving the right, and rain falling in the two shaded bands either side of the funnel — cyclonic rainfall.
Figure (B), left-hand column of p-58 — the orographic cross-section. Needed to read which slope of the mountain (windward vs leeward) carries the heavier rain.
Figure (B), left-hand column of p-58 — the same orographic cross-section. Needed so the student can shade the leeward-side region beyond the crest and name it the rain-shadow area.
Figure (A) on p-57 (convectional: rain with upward-pointing arrows) — one half of the A-vs-C comparison this question asks for.
Figure (C) on p-58 (cyclonic: spiral with horizontal in/out arrows and rain bands) — the other half of the A-vs-C comparison.
Figure (C) on p-58 — the cyclone picture the student must pick out of the A/B/C set as the rainfall type associated with stormy winds and floods.

Figure (A) on p-57 — the convectional picture the student must pick out of the A/B/C set as the equatorial (Singapore) rainfall type. Q3 is printed under 'Look at the figures above and answer', so all five sub-items read off the same A/B/C set.
Figures (B) and (C) on p-58 — the two rival options the student rules out when choosing the Singapore rainfall type from the A/B/C set.
